name: workflow
tagline: Cron, delayed jobs, background queues and multi-step workflows for Go, behind one interface
description: Embeddable Go library for cron schedules, delayed and background jobs with retries, and multi-step workflows behind one Client interface, with swappable drivers: in-memory, SQL (SQLite, Postgres, MySQL 8) and Hatchet. Each driver declares its capabilities and a shared conformance suite proves them.

positioning.category: Go job queue, scheduler and workflow library
positioning.audience: Go developers building product backends (SaaS, sync pipelines, webhook delivery, notifications) and desktop or CLI apps that need a scheduler on an embedded SQLite file
positioning.wedge: Every Go app rebuilds cron, a job queue, retries and multi-step workflows, and each library it picks locks it into one backend. ubgo/workflow puts them behind one interface, so the same handlers run in memory in tests, on SQLite, Postgres or MySQL in production, or on Hatchet, and a backend that cannot do something says so instead of faking it.
differentiators: One Client interface for schedules, jobs and workflows, with in-memory, SQL and Hatchet drivers
Honest capabilities: Start refuses a workflow that needs a capability the driver lacks, and an unsupported field returns ErrUnsupported naming it
A shared conformance suite every driver runs, plus multi-client tests on the SQL driver: each step claimed once, one cron tick per schedule across three clients, a dead worker's lease reclaimed
SQLite, Postgres and MySQL 8 on database/sql through ubgo/sqlb, with versioned migrations and transactional enqueue inside the app's own transaction
Own cron parser evaluated in an explicit time zone, and an injected clock for tests
Standard-library-only core, enforced by a dependency guard test
Batches with callbacks, unique and debounced jobs, claim check for big payloads, failover between backends, a transactional outbox and OpenTelemetry middleware as optional packages
